title: MARCH: Model-Assisted Reinforcement Learning for the Perceptive Control of Humanoids over Sparse Footholds
summary: Vision-guided humanoid locomotion over sparse footholds, combining model-based foothold planning with learned control.

media.alt: Unitree G1 traversing laterally constrained stepping stones; accompanying depth observations from the experiment.
media.caption: Physical Unitree G1 experiment and corresponding depth observations. Figure 1 from the MARCH paper.

video.caption: Full MARCH demonstration: method overview, simulation comparisons, and physical Unitree G1 experiments.

methods.label: Model-assisted planning
methods.detail: Generate safe reference trajectories with a model-based foothold planner to guide learned locomotion control.

methods.label: Teacher training
methods.detail: PPO with domain randomization in a MuJoCo/mjlab pipeline running 4,096 parallel simulation environments.

methods.label: Perceptive student policy
methods.detail: Distill the teacher into a CNN–transformer–mixture-density-network policy using depth images and proprioceptive observations.

results.label: Teacher-training episodes
results.context: 10,000 episodes versus 20,000 for the model-free baseline.

results.label: Less joint torque
results.context: Mean absolute joint torque versus the model-free baseline.

results.label: Less angular jerk
results.context: Mean absolute angular jerk versus the model-free baseline.

research.evaluationNote: Torque and jerk comparisons use 2,048 simulated student-policy rollouts after 500 distillation iterations. These are simulation results, not physical-robot success rates.
